package.name: statgrab
package.summary: PHP bindings for libstatgrab: CPU, memory, disk, network, and process metrics.
package.description:
PHP bindings for libstatgrab (https://libstatgrab.org), the cross-platform system-statistics library. Reads CPU usage, memory and swap, disk I/O, filesystem space and inode counts, network interface counters, page-in/out, process tables, logged-in users, and host metadata. Works on glibc Linux, musl, macOS, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD, and Solaris.
Two API surfaces ship in parallel: a procedural one matching the original 2006 PECL release (sg_cpu_percent_usage, sg_memory_stats, sg_process_stats, ...) and a Statgrab class with method-based access and class constants for sort orders, process states, and duplex modes. Both surfaces emit E_WARNING and return false on libstatgrab errors; the OO surface throws on argument-count violations. sg_error_details() returns array{code,errno,message,arg} from libstatgrab (or false when no error is pending); the OO surface exposes the same shape via Statgrab::errorDetails().
The repo also ships a vendored libstatgrab 0.92.2, which fixes memory-safety bugs that distribution 0.92.1 packages still carry, with local patches for two undefined shifts, a lost mount-table error, a crash when a thread exits after the extension unloads, and regex lookups that resolve to oniguruma instead of glibc. Configure with --with-statgrab=bundled to statically link the patched copy without waiting on system packages.
Requires libstatgrab >= 0.92 and PHP >= 8.0 (NTS or ZTS).
package.notes:
ZTS, FrankenPHP worker mode, and bundled-library fixes.
- Under ZTS on glibc, an sg_fs_stats() call stalled on a hung mount no longer blocks other threads' sg_fs_stats() and sg_valid_filesystems(). - A thread that used statgrab no longer crashes on exit after the host unloads the extension. - sg_error_details() no longer reports an error from an earlier request on the same thread, including in FrankenPHP worker mode. - Bundled libstatgrab reports a mount-table open failure from sg_fs_stats(), and always uses glibc's regex when PHP links oniguruma. - On PHP 8.5.12+ and 8.6, a result that outgrows memory_limit ends with the memory-limit fatal error instead of exit status 137.
See CHANGELOG.md for the full list.
